mentions.name: UPSS (Universal Prompt Security Standard)
mentions.description: An open-source framework for managing LLM prompts securely at scale. It externalizes prompts from application code via secure configuration management, provides a modular middleware architecture with composable security primitives (BasicSanitizer, LightweightAuditor, SimpleRBAC, InputValidator), and delivers complete audit trails and version control with approval workflows. Version 1.1.0 ships a Python implementation plus examples for Node.js, Java, Go, and Rust, and the project seeks community contributions for security primitives, framework integrations, language implementations, and adoption stories.
mentions.problem: Most organizations hardcode prompts directly into application code, creating security vulnerabilities (90% prompt injection success rate in typical deployments), operational inefficiency (3-5 day deployment cycles for simple prompt changes), and compliance gaps (insufficient audit trails for SOC 2, ISO 27001).
mentions.audience: Startups and enterprises needing practical, not theoretical, security for LLM prompts
